key_insight: Stoichiometry-preserved ionic clusters can act as predictive stand-ins for unknown crystal structures, enabling few-shot property prediction for multi-ionic energetic materials.
engineering_relevance: This offers a pre-synthesis screening route that can prioritize promising compositions before full crystal-structure determination, reducing experimental and computational cost.
method: Represent each candidate as a non-periodic, formula-unit ionic cluster that preserves stoichiometry.
Fine-tune a pretrained machine-learned interatomic potential with multi-task energy/force regularization.
Use the learned surrogate to screen detonation velocity for new compositions without retraining on the target materials.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation on 25 curated perovskite-type energetic materials showed predictive detonation-velocity screening, and the model transferred to three new ABX4 materials with a reported MAE of 92 m·s^-1.
watch_item: The approach is trained on a very small, curated dataset, so generalization may be sensitive to coverage of chemistry and cluster construction choices.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
